assessments.summary: Measles cases in the US are peaking with a 232% increase in weekly reports compared to the previous 8 months, totaling 4,628 cases this year versus 1,544 at the same time last year.
Dengue cases in the US are peaking with a 533% increase in weekly reports compared to the previous 8 months, totaling 1,202 cases this year versus 1,273 at the same time last year.
West Nile virus cases in the US are peaking with a 1,762% increase in weekly reports compared to the previous 8 months, totaling 1,611 cases this year versus 2,619 at the same time last year.
Ebola cases are peaking with a high case fatality ratio of 48.7% in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, and Nigeria, where 10,668 confirmed cases have been reported.
Influenza cases are peaking with a 76% increase in US hospital admissions compared to the previous month and a 12% rise in global flu test positivity.
Legionnaires' disease cases in the US are rising with a 79% increase in weekly reports compared to the previous 8 months, totaling 7,692 cases this year versus 8,313 at the same time last year.
Mpox cases in the US are rising with a 47% increase in weekly reports compared to the previous 8 months, totaling 1,434 cases this year versus 2,018 at the same time last year.
Malaria cases in the US are rising with a 59% increase in weekly reports compared to the previous 8 months, totaling 1,130 cases this year versus 1,400 at the same time last year.

RSV activity is at baseline with no significant increase in hospitalizations or test positivity compared to the previous month, though US hospital admissions have risen sharply over the past 8 months.
Pertussis cases in the US are rising sharply, with a 48% increase in reported cases over the past 8 months and a significant jump in annual cases.
US COVID-19 hospital admissions are slightly higher than the previous month, but activity remains at baseline with low public interest.
Marburg virus disease activity is falling with low public interest, as evidenced by Wikipedia readership.
Chikungunya cases in the US are stable with a slight decrease over the past 8 months, though annual cases have increased modestly.
Norovirus activity remains at baseline with moderate public interest.
Avian influenza activity is at baseline with low public interest.
